title: Golden replay
description: One recorded game. The ground truth a reimplementation validates against. Randomness is carried as a recorded random_log rather than a seed, so replaying never depends on matching the studio's RNG, shuffle algorithm or draw order. See reference/04-golden-replays.md

coverage_tags.description: Why this replay is in the corpus: bespoke_cards, trigger_collision, deck_out, longest_game, mirror, ...

deck.description: Card ids in pre-shuffle order. The resulting order comes from random_log, not from a seed.

instance.description: Card instance id, stable across the game

choices.description: Resolution of any choice point this action opens

state_hash_after.description: Strongly recommended after EVERY action. Cheap, and localizes a divergence to the exact action that caused it.

verification.description: Filled by the generating studio. A replay shipped without passing verification is a determinism bug, not a replay.

random_log.description: Every random decision the engine made, in the order it made them. This is what replaces a seed: the rebuilt engine consumes these outcomes instead of generating its own, so the shuffle algorithm and draw count become irrelevant. A seedable or single-source RNG is NOT required -- only the ability to log what came out.

where.description: Stable label for the call site, e.g. 'setup.shuffle.p0' or 'card.bolt.damage_roll'. Strongly recommended: when a rebuild drifts, this names the decision point where control flow parted, which is a better clue than a mismatched end state.

result.description: What came out. For permutation, the resulting order (or indices).

range.description: For kind=int, the inclusive [lo, hi] the engine drew from. REQUIRED in practice: a recorded 2 falls inside both [1,3] and [1,4], so without the declared range a rebuild can reproduce every replay perfectly and still generate out-of-distribution games during training. This field is what prevents a simulator that looks correct and is not.

p.description: For kind=bool, the probability. Same reasoning as range.

options_count.description: For kind=choice, how many options were offered.

state_dumps.description: Serialized state at the start, after each turn, and at the end. Optional -- replays work without it, but a divergence can then only be localized to the whole game.
